articles.title: The Batman Part 2 Set Photos Hint at Arkham-Style Batsuit Upgrade
articles.summary: Some possible spoilers about The Batman: Part II may be revealed in these set photos. New photos from the Glasgow set of The Batman: Part II reveal a closer look at the Dark Knight’s updated batsuit in the sequel.
body: The armor appears to be darker and shinier than it was in The Batman, while the cowl’s ears are a bit longer. Most notable is the addition of a mustard-colored utility belt.
Other fans claim, however, that the suit isn’t noticeably darker or shinier than it was in the 2022 film and that it may just be the result of the way the set is lit.
Robert Pattinson’s stunt double Rick English can be seen in costume in the set photos.
Some photos show a bloodied Batman who then commandeers a Gotham City Police motorcycle and escapes by ramping off the hood of a GCPD car.

articles.title: How to Navigate Rebecca Yarros' Popular Fourth Wing Book Series
articles.summary: Rebecca Yarros has been writing romance novels for more than a decade now, but it's her popular romantasy series that has truly caught fire. Fourth Wing, the first book in the Empyrean series, is a spicy story about a dragon academy and magic.
body: If you're new to the Empyrean series or romantasy in general, starting with Fourth Wing is an excellent choice. Rebecca Yarros is also coming out with a companion book this year called Threshing Day, which takes place across different points in the book timeline.

There are a ton of different ways to enjoy books these days, and the Empyrean series is available in pretty much every format. If you don't care about reading physical books, I'd suggest checking out the Kindle versions first. The Fourth Wing books absolutely dominated the Kindle charts last year with the release of Onyx Storm, and reading digitally is by far the most convenient way to enjoy the story. That being said, the paperback and hardcover editions are similarly priced.

If you prefer to listen to audiobooks, the original version narrated by Rebecca Soler has received rather mixed reviews online. For the best possible experience, you'll want to check out the dramatized adaptations of the first book. These feature a full cast and offer a much richer experience.
points: Rebecca Yarros has been writing romance novels for more than a decade now, but it's her popular romantasy series that has truly caught fire.

articles.title: The 5 Best Games That Still Aren't Officially Available in the US
articles.summary: Right now, we have unprecedented access to video games. Platforms like Steam offer tremendous access to AAA and indie titles alike, while services like Nintendo Switch Online are bringing plenty of classic titles to modern hardware.
body: But a ton of games are still unavailable for gamers all over the world. Plenty of popular, influential, and acclaimed titles never got English localizations. Translation issues, timing, and censorship all prevented these five games from officially reaching Western audiences, though that may not have stopped fan translators.

Atlus’ Megami Tensei franchise, from which Shin Megami Tensei, Devil Summoner, and Persona all spun off, is one of the most pivotal franchises in JRPG history. But its very first release never officially reached Western audiences. Digital Devil Story: Megami Tense i, a role-playing dungeon crawler for the Famicom, follows high school student Akemi Nakajima, who uses a computer program to summon demons. As expected, this does not go well, and Nakajima and his girlfriend have to bring down the forces of Lucifer.

Digital Devil Story: Megami Tensei had slim chances of getting an English translation. To maintain a family-friendly image, Nintendo of America had a strict (though not always consistently applied) policy of censoring religious references in games, including symbols related to Satan. A game where you fight the Biblical devil never really stood a chance.
points: Right now, we have unprecedented access to video games.
Platforms like Steam offer tremendous access to AAA and indie titles alike, while services like Nintendo Switch Online are bringing plenty of classic titles to modern hardware.
But a ton of games are still unavailable for gamers all over the world.
Translation issues, timing, and censorship all prevented these five games from officially reaching Western audiences, though that may not have stopped fan translators.

articles.title: Bruce Campbell Says He Has 5 Years Left to Live Amid Cancer Battle
articles.summary: Evil Dead star Bruce Campbell said he has just five years left to live amid his ongoing battle with cancer. The legendary horror actor gave fans an update on his health during an appearance on The Adam Carolla Show earlier this week.
body: "In my world, I'm in a five-year prognosis," Campbell said. "The type of cancer I have, which I don't want to get into, the current thing is a five-year deal."
The show's host then asked the 68-year-old actor for clarification, questioning if that meant he had five years left to live.

The actor announced his cancer diagnosis in March of this year, confirming that convention appearances and work in general would "take a back seat to treatment." He added at the time that he was "a tough old son-of-a-bitch" and that he expected "to be around for a while."

During the new interview, Campbell admitted there are plenty of stories of others fighting cancer who outlive their initial timelines, adding that medical technology could become more advanced during his own fight. For him, though, the real battle is "to live with it, not die from it."

articles.title: Asus ROG Swift OLED PG27UCWM Review
articles.summary: The Asus ROG Swift OLED PG27UCWM offers a gorgeous display that works as well for cinematic games as it does for competitive, fast-paced ones.
body: Asus didn’t leave much out when it designed the ROG Swift OLED PG27UCWM. That said, it doesn’t have speakers, but you’ll find it checks boxes in just about every other department.

The PG27UCWM is ready for a lot of cables, too. You’ll find two HDMI 2.1 ports, a DisplayPort 2.1a port, and even a capable USB-C port that’ll take in video and send out up to 90 watts of power. There are two USB ports for passing data to a connected system, letting the monitor serve as a USB hub as well with a KVM switch so you can pass that connection to the USB-C link or a separate USB-B link. If you want to connect speakers, there’s a headphone jack, too.

Around back, the PG27UCWM spices things up a little. Rather than the classic black ABS plastic you’ll find on half the monitors in the world, the PG27UCWM opts for a transparent plastic that gives it something of a cyberpunk aesthetic. It may still feel like cheap plastic, but it looks damn good.

Another feature is a presence sensor that can help preserve the lifespan of the OLED panel by dimming it whenever you step away. I didn’t find it overly sensitive, so I wasn’t concerned it’d blink off while I’m in the middle of a game.
points: The Asus ROG Swift OLED PG27UCWM offers a gorgeous display that works as well for cinematic games as it does for competitive, fast-paced ones.

articles.title: Double Fine reveals its first post-Xbox game as Tim Schafer declares no one will shut the studio down but him
articles.summary: Double Fine, which regained independence from Xbox Game Studios in July, has unveiled its first post-Xbox game: Thank You Bus Driver. Studio founder Tim Schafer declared in a recent interview that his studio will keep making weird games like it and Keeper, as no one will be able to shut down Double…
body: In August, the San Francisco-based studio unveiled a new label called Double Fine Action Labs. Inspired by recent indie hits like Peak, Double Fine Action Labs will focus on smaller-scale titles that can be quickly announced and released for players. Thank You Bus Driver will be the first game released under that label, and it fits the bill perfectly.

Thank You Bus Driver is a quirky take on a transportation simulator game where players have to chaotically pick up and drive passengers while also paying attention to what they're doing and slapping them if they break a rule. It's something I can't imagine Xbox Game Studios publishing anymore, making it a perfect declaration of the kinds of games neo-Double Fine is interested in developing.

articles.title: 'We Are Sorry,' Gamescom Apologizes For Lackluster Response To Indie Booth Thefts
articles.summary: After severe backlash to its initial response to reports of theft at Gamescom 2026, Gamescom has now issued an apology with several promises that it will hopefully keep.
body: Gamescom 's first response to overnight thefts at numerous indie booths was nothing short of disappointing. Instead of providing compensation and support, it focused on victim-blaming and imposing additional security services. Its latest statement is a lot more apologetic in tone and promises a "dedicated review of security for indie exhibitors" and to hold a developer roundtable for feedback.

"Our first response did not strike the right tone, and it did not show the people affected the empathy they deserved. We are sorry," Gamescom wrote. "A theft like this is more than a material loss...To everyone affected: we understand what this has cost you, and we should have said so from the very first moment. We have already begun talking with those affected — about theft, about its consequences, and above all to listen."

Regardless of Gamescom's apology, many in the comments section still expressed their discontent with the organization. It's clear that the thefts and the lack of effort to solve them initially may have greatly damaged some fans' opinions of Gamescom.
points: After severe backlash to its initial response to reports of theft at Gamescom 2026, Gamescom has now issued an apology with several promises that it will hopefully keep.

articles.title: Xbox Cloud Gaming's new hourly cap is reportedly set exactly where Microsoft stops making money on it
articles.summary: A new report suggests that Xbox has capped its cloud gaming usage to 15 hours for Game Pass Ultimate subscribers because that's when the service stops being profitable.
body: According to Windows Central, which cites unnamed Microsoft sources, that's not an arbitrary cap and is, allegedly, set at Microsoft's own break-even threshold as any usage beyond that costs the company money.

Windows Central ties the cost pressure to a wider squeeze on server memory caused by Microsoft's AI investments, with Azure capacity increasingly prioritised for AI workloads over game streaming. It frames the caps as part of a broader cost-cutting pattern across Xbox, alongside recent layoffs and cancelled projects, as the division comes under pressure to turn a bigger profit.

As Connor reported for us in the week, according to a 2025 report from Statista, US gamers spent an average of 9.5 hours per week playing video games, UK gamers 6.38 hours, and a worldwide average of 6.56 hours was recorded.
Despite Xbox scaling back its cloud gaming plans and the seemingly endless issues caused by the ramping up of AI data centres, industry giants remain bullish on cloud gaming.

articles.title: 2026 Has Been the Best Year for City-Builders in Decades
articles.summary: I picked the best possible year to get deep into city builders, at least in terms of being spoiled for high-quality choices. Having the time to play them all? Yeah, that's another matter entirely.
body: After years in early access, the 1.0 version of Mechanistry's whimsical Timberborn finally launched in March. I call it whimsical because it simply couldn’t fit more whimsy into it: You’re a beaver planner building a giant beaver city. It's a crunchy management sim nonetheless. You're managing water flow via aqueducts and dams (what else?) and making the most of limited space on your island, which means building up once the lateral space runs out. Once you get used to the early game learning curve, the real challenge is making the most of that limited space.

Speaking of water, the excellent Nova Roma finally entered early access earlier this year, too. It's a bit like Anno 117 -lite. You set up a little Roman town and turn it into a big city by establishing production chains and meeting the needs of your adorable, tiny citizens. Most of this happens through carefully managing the flow of water and reacting to sudden changes in the weather. Sometimes, it's just nature being nature. Sometimes, it's because you pissed the gods off. They're very opinionated in Nova Roma.
A weekly cheat sheet to what you’ll eventually love to play. No buying, no commitment — just saving for later.
points: I picked the best possible year to get deep into city builders, at least in terms of being spoiled for high-quality choices.

articles.title: Sony clarifies PlayStation disc production is dropping by 10 percent in 2028, not to 10 percent
articles.summary: Sony has pushed back on a wave of reports suggesting PlayStation disc manufacturing is about to be gutted by 90 percent after comments from a Sony DADC executive were allegedly misunderstood.
body: According to Game, which went directly to Sony Digital Audio Disc Corporation (DADC) for clarity, output is actually expected to dip by 10 percent in 2028, not to 10 percent.

"To clarify and avoid any misleading information: in that statement Dietmar anticipated an overall product volume decline by 10 percent, not a decline down to 10 percent," a Sony DADC spokesperson told Game, referring to comments made by DADC chief Dietmar Tanzer to an Austrian broadcaster in July.
The spokesperson didn't say what happens beyond 2028, and directed further questions on reorders to PlayStation's own PR team, which didn't respond to Game's queries.

The confusion stems from PlayStation's July announcement that it will stop producing physical discs for new games from January 2028 onward, though already-released titles and games still slated for disc release before that date aren't affected, and reorders will continue afterwards.

articles.title: Before HBO’s The Last Of Us, An Entirely Different Adaptation Was Proposed
articles.summary: Naughty Dog's first effort to adapt The Last of Us for the screen was not as an HBO TV show, but a movie, a fact that recently began doing the rounds again on social media.
body: While not everyone agrees with the creative departures from the source material for the TV series on HBO, it's undeniably a success and one of HBO's biggest hits lately. Let's look back at how The Last of Us originated as a movie and run through the key developments that led to it becoming a TV show.
People across X recently discovered a post from Sony Pictures in 2014 declaring that The Last of Us was "soon to be a major motion picture."

This was a real, studio-sponsored image, not a fan mock-up. There was officially produced key art, showing Ellie wielding a knife. There was a "secret panel" at San Diego Comic-Con that year featuring director Sam Raimi, who was originally attached to produce the movie, having already had huge success at Sony with his Spider-Man films.
That The Last of Us was originally going to be a movie is not surprising given how many video game movies came before it and how many have been released since (with varying degrees of success).

articles.title: Saber CCO Tim Willits blames layoffs on games industry overspecialization: 'Studios that have a couple hundred employees that work on one game are going to struggle'
articles.summary: With mega-games like GTA 6 on the way, it's hard not to feel like games are always getting bigger—both the software itself, and the teams that make it (GTA 6 has an entire dedicated NPC team "art-directing" its every background character).
body: "The industry always has some cycles, some ups and downs, and one of the things that we have done well to avoid some of the issues that other studios have had is we spread out our resources," Willits said. "We develop games that are across the scope spectrum, for lack of a better description." While games like Space Marine 2 and the upcoming Jurassic Park: Survival take a lot of manpower, the studio relies on remasters and smaller games to fund those "big bets."

"We have a culture where people can work on any game, and we can move resources around. So we avoid the 'silo problem' that you find with big studios," he continued. "Studios that have a couple hundred employees that work on one game are going to struggle. They're going to really struggle to survive. Because before a game hits a vertical slice, you do not need hundreds of people on that."

He noted that if there's a studio culture where nimble developers can realize smaller passion projects, those can then turn out to be big hits unexpectedly—an example he gave was SnowRunner, a "mega franchise" for Saber with over 46,000 user reviews on Steam. That started as "an experiment by one guy."

articles.title: Gamescom apologises for how it initially responded to indie developer hardware thefts
articles.summary: Gamescom has apologised for the way it "communicated about the theft of hardware belonging to several indie developers" last week, admitting, "our first response did not strike the right tone, and it did not show the people affected the empathy they deserved".
body: Multiple exhibitors at Gamescom reported thefts of laptops and other equipment from their booths in Cologne last week, with one indie developer, Ryan Laley, saying the loss has effectively ended his show early. Iam8bit also reported two of its laptops were taken overnight from the same business area, as did Tessera Studios.
Addressing the thefts at the time, Gamescom said it was "aware of stolen hardware" and understood "the frustration of affected exhibitors", triggering further condemnation from attendees.

Now, in a new statement posted yesterday (4th September), Gamescom posted a follow-up statement on social media, saying the organisers "understand what this has cost you, and we should have said so from the very first moment".

A theft like this is far more than a material loss. It can ruin an entire Gamescom for the people it happens to, and it can destroy work that took months or years to build - work that, for a small studio, can be almost everything. To everyone affected: we understand what this has cost you, and we should have said so from the very first moment.

articles.title: Kingdom Come: Deliverance director says DLSS 5 does right by KCD 2, 'people are crazy' for thinking it's AI slop
articles.summary: DLSS 5 is a controversial technology for all sorts of reasons —you might have heard about this little thing called AI slop—but perhaps the most infamous is its uncanny look.
body: Director of both Kingdom Come: Deliverance games, Daniel Vávra, has re-entered this battle on the side of DLSS 5. Last Sunday, he took to X to say that some critics of the tech have "literally gone crazy," providing a before-and-after comparison with KCD 2 to say that it indeed helped realize the team's vision.

"On the left is a head messed up by the game engine’s very limited lighting system, which can’t properly render shadows, skin texture, and the detail of normal maps," he wrote, saying the DLSS 5'd version had improved details. "Having no shadows from helmets on faces and fucked up normal map rendering WAS NOT OUR ORIGINAL ARTISTIC VISION."

It's worth noting concerns about AI revising art aren't necessarily about whether it can technically touch up blemishes for a cleaner end product—I'm sure AI would cut Paul McCartney hitting a wrong chord and mumbling "fucking hell" out of Hey Jude if it could, but surely we can agree that little mistake makes the song better. The occasional flub signals the art's humanity. Still, some folks on X were quick to argue against Vávra's point that it was an improvement at all.

articles.title: BioWare doesn't need advice for Mass Effect 4, says veteran designer, as long as "people get out of the way"
articles.summary: Original Mass Effect cinematic designer and Mass Effect 2 lead cinematic designer Armando Troisi has insisted the current BioWare team doesn't need outside advice on developing the next installment because so many of the people who built the original trilogy are still at the studio.
body: Asked what guidance they'd offer developers working on the new game, Troisi didn't think they had anything to add.

"It's hard for me to say because a lot of people that are on that project were there [during the originals]," Troisi told FRVR. "They know. Preston [Watamaniuk] is there, and Derek [Watts] is there, and Parish [Ley] is there, and they're the OGs, you know? I don't think there's anything that I could tell them that they don't know what to do."
Troisi left the studio after Mass Effect 2, but has confident in the team that remains behind.

"When I was leaving, everybody wrote on a card… he [Preston] said, 'passion and craft is excellence'… I think they've got both of those so I don't think that I can give them any more advice than they already have. They know this stuff," Troisi said.

body: But smooshing three distinct eras of Tomb Raider into one broad continuity is a difficult task that makes for some questionable choices. Tomb Raider: Legacy of Atlantis gameplay grafts baffling survival mechanics onto a classic '90s adventure, while a composite of Laras leads to some dizzying tonal whiplash. And, the studio's controversial use of generative AI in development raises some eyebrows, leaving crucial pieces of in-game art looking very suspect.
